clue.text: Chap's first to give lots to girl? Not him

definitions.text: Chap's first to give lots to girl? Not him

indicators.note: first here asks for only the opening letter of the word Chap's

parts.note: heaps means lots, a great many
Kate is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A riddle about which man would not shower a girlfriend with gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes the initial letter of Chap's. The whole clue also describes the answer: a mean man is the one who would not give lots to a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A miserly person is exactly the sort who would refuse to lavish money on a date.

clue.text: The charm of the footplate?

parts.note: suggests the appeal of a locomotive driver's platform, but means the lucky emblem that is literally a plate nailed to a hoof

explanation.definitionFit: A curved iron hoof plate is hung over doors as a lucky charm.

clue.text: Factor that's secret in Conrad's work

definitions.meaning: a factor is someone who acts on another's behalf, a representative
Joseph Conrad's novel is The Secret ...

explanation.definitionFit: A factor is a business representative, and Joseph Conrad wrote The Secret Agent.

clue.text: Valuable ointment I know is in box with key

indicators.note: is in means the first pieces go inside the word for box

parts.note: to spar is to box
taken as written
ken is Scots for know
D is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone recognises a costly balm kept in a locked box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in' sets I plus the Scots word for know inside the boxing verb; the musical key follows. Spikenard was the costly ointment of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Spikenard was a costly aromatic balm prized in the ancient world.

clue.text: Apart from a place up North, deprived of land

indicators.note: deprived of means the following word's letters are taken away

parts.note: Sunderland is a city in north-east England
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone apart from a northern town has lost their land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deprived of' strips LAND from SUNDERLAND, a city in north-east England, leaving SUNDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Asunder means into separate pieces, apart.

clue.text: Bird's cry, moving East

indicators.note: moving means one letter of the word for cry shifts to another position

parts.note: greet is Scots for weep, cry
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A bird's call travels eastward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' takes the second E of GREET to the front. 'Greet' is a Scottish word for weep.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white heron, a wading bird.

clue.text: Get ready for change, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to turn a cheque into money is to obtain ready money, 'ready' being slang for money
loose coins, or change, are an example of money in hand

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means convert a cheque to banknotes; as a noun it means money, of which small change is one kind.

clue.text: Cleaner city beat fraud

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a cleaner
LA is Los Angeles
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: A cleaner in a city overcomes a swindler.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is a British word for a cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlatan is a fraud who claims skills they lack.

clue.text: Having lost warm coat, but having second cape

parts.note: Cape Horn, so horn can mean cape

explanation.surface: Someone loses a warm coat but has a spare cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cape' is the headland, Cape Horn, not a cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheep that is shorn has had its fleece clipped off.

clue.text: In place of prayer, had rude questions — that's socially acceptable

parts.note: pried means snooped with nosy questions
i.e. stands for 'that is'
U means upper-class, socially acceptable

explanation.surface: Someone at a place of worship asked rude questions, yet behaved acceptably.
explanation.walkthrough: IE is the abbreviation for 'that is'; U is the old label for upper-class usage, coined by Nancy Mitford's circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A prie-dieu is a kneeling desk at which a person says their devotions.

clue.text: Study endlessly, boy, and think

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for study loses its final letter

parts.note: to read is to study
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Advice to a boy to keep studying and to think.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the D from READ, leaving REA.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason is to work something out by logical thought.

clue.text: Show anger in article on bishop's responsibility

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: a see is the diocese a bishop is responsible for
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone shows anger in a newspaper article about a bishop's duties.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer 'on' means placed after. A bishop's see is his diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to be inwardly furious, boiling with rage.

clue.text: Where day-to-day changes occur

parts.note: reads as daily alterations, but means the line across the Pacific where the calendar date jumps by one

explanation.definitionFit: Crossing the international meridian of that name moves the calendar forward or back a day.

clue.text: Attempt by golfer to make the cut

definitions.meaning: a short lofted shot onto the green is a golf stroke of this name
to knock a small piece off something is to cut it

explanation.definitionFit: A golfer plays a lofted approach shot of this name, and to break off a fragment is to cut.

clue.text: Detail payment required for management of circulation

parts.note: a point is a detail, an item
a duty is a tax that must be paid

explanation.surface: A list of required payments for running a business's circulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulation' is traffic flow, directed by a police officer on point duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Point duty is a police officer's job of directing traffic at a junction.

clue.text: Basic act or complicated gymnastic performance

indicators.note: complicated tells us the preceding words are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A simple routine or a complex gymnastic display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complicated' rearranges BASIC ACT OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumbling, somersaults and balancing feats make up this gymnastic display.

clue.text: Physical examination that prevents progress in sport

definitions.meaning: a check of the body, a medical
in ice hockey, blocking an opponent with the body

explanation.definitionFit: A medical inspection of the body, and in ice hockey a legal block on an opposing player.

clue.text: Dependants spoiling a rest cure

indicators.note: spoiling means the following words are damaged into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Dependants ruin someone's peaceful recuperation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoiling' rearranges A REST CURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature in the old sense is someone's dependent protégé or puppet.

clue.text: Astonished playwright about to be accepted by foundation

indicators.note: to be accepted by means the playwright and 'about' go inside the foundation word

parts.note: a bed is a foundation, as in a bed of concrete
Oscar Wilde was an Irish playwright
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A dramatist is amazed to win acceptance from a charitable foundation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be accepted by' sets the Irish playwright plus 'about' inside the foundation word, between its first two letters and its last.
explanation.definitionFit: Bewildered means utterly confused or amazed.

clue.text: Formal procedure that's legally binding

parts.note: reads as an enforceable process, but also hints at the coloured ribbon once used to tie up lawyers' papers

explanation.definitionFit: Bureaucratic rules are named after the ribbon that bound official documents.

clue.text: Refrain from seasonal performance

parts.note: reads as abstaining from a Christmas show, but means the repeated chorus word of a Christmas carol

explanation.definitionFit: The Christmas carol repeats this word, meaning Christmas, as its chorus.

clue.text: Superficially damaged, continued without operation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the abbreviation for continued surrounds the other word

parts.note: contd is the standard abbreviation for continued
use means operation, as in 'in use'

explanation.surface: Something was bruised but kept going without surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' carries its old meaning of outside: the abbreviation for continued goes round the word for operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Contused means bruised, injured without the skin being broken.

clue.text: Provide view from old wood

parts.note: pine is a kind of wood

explanation.surface: Someone gives an opinion about some old timber.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state an opinion.

clue.text: Cancel contribution, being in credit? On the contrary

indicators.note: being in sets one piece inside another, contribution inside credit as the surface reads
On the contrary reverses that order, so credit goes inside contribution instead

parts.note: a sub, or subscription, is a contribution

explanation.surface: Someone cancels a donation because their account is in credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being in' alone would put the contribution inside credit; 'On the contrary' flips that, so credit goes inside the contribution.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub a plan is to call it off.

clue.text: Truman's finest bill sent back by Senate at last

definitions.note: a possessive standing for the surname that belongs to Truman

indicators.note: sent back means the two pieces together are read backwards

parts.note: top means best, finest
AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: at last picks out only the final letter of Senate

explanation.surface: President Truman's best bill was returned by the Senate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns TOPAC into CAPOT; then the E ending Senate. The surface wants President Truman, but it is the author Truman Capote.
explanation.definitionFit: Truman Capote was the American author of In Cold Blood, so the surname is the one Truman bore.

clue.text: Move to next page, holding scripture for primate

indicators.note: holding means the first piece contains the second

parts.note: PTO, please turn over, tells a reader to move to the next page
OT is the Old Testament, scripture

explanation.surface: An instruction to turn the page while keeping hold of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: PTO is written at the foot of a page: please turn over.
explanation.definitionFit: The potto is a slow-moving African primate.

clue.text: Drink is sweet, without ice

indicators.note: without here means taking away the letters of the following word

parts.note: liquorice is a black confection, a sweet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drink is sweet when served with no ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes ICE from LIQUORICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquor is alcoholic drink, especially spirits.

clue.text: Politician on a school governing body is quite unpredictable

indicators.note: in an across answer, the politician placed on the other pieces follows them

parts.note: LEA stands for Local Education Authority, the British council body that ran schools
a Tory is a Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A politician sitting on a school board behaves erratically.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer 'on' means placed after. A Local Education Authority was a British council's schools body.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleatory means depending on chance, hence wholly unpredictable.

clue.text: Raise money in Bulgaria and Japan

parts.note: the lev is the currency of Bulgaria
Japan's money is the yen, abbreviated Y

explanation.surface: A fundraising drive in two countries, Bulgaria and Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'money' serves both countries: the Bulgarian lev and the Japanese yen, written Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To levy a tax is to impose and collect it, so to raise funds.

clue.text: Book dismal accommodation

parts.note: bleak means dismal, cheerless
a house is accommodation, a place to live

explanation.surface: A review dismissing grim lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a novel by Charles Dickens.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleak House is a novel by Charles Dickens.
